decisions.reason: As a still-recent handle family in the firm's core architectural hardware range, the sunk development and launch effort plus portfolio fit make management likely to continue backing it absent clear evidence of failure.

This mitred handle family remains closely aligned with the firm's design-led positioning, so prior investment and the need to justify the launch favor retention despite some rising review pressure after two years.

Because the multifunctional concept supports the firm's stated barrier-free and system-solution direction, management would be inclined to interpret any mixed uptake as temporary and keep it on the market.
Another lever-handle family in the firm's established competence area is likely to be retained because accumulated engineering, tooling and sales effort encourage continuation rather than reversal.
The dedicated public presentation and design-award recognition create the strongest visible commitment of all the launches, making withdrawal within the coming year very unlikely.

The light patinated bronze finish is the easiest item to rationalize away because it is a finish rather than a full family, but management would still likely keep it as part of the broader design and materials offering unless demand clearly disappoints.
